publications.title: Worker Balancing Implementation on DRAGON Scheduler for Distributed Deep Learning in Kubernetes
publications.description: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that usually has more computation and uses a bigger dataset. The data size and model complexity that is used by deep learning itself tends to increase over time. This leads to an increase in training duration. One method to solve this issue is to use distributed deep learning to divide computation loads among several machines. One method to do distributed deep learning is by using DRAGON scheduler that adapts parameter server architecture by implementing it on Kubernetes and Tensorflow. DRAGON scheduler is developed from the tf-operator controller in Kubeflow and has some advantages such as locality-aware placement and load-aware scaling. Unfortunately, such features still do not address parameter server limitations well, which makes scaling on training jobs with a high number of workers is not effective. So, to avoid this limitation, a worker-balancing approach is used. By implementing this approach, the training duration of the DRAGON scheduler can be reduced to 16.31% compared to the original without reducing its prediction accuracy. Show less
